question.problem:
$$
f(x)∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)
$$

Let $F(x)=7{x}^{2}+4$ for $x\in [0,\pi ).$ The Fourier cosine series of the **even** $2\pi $-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is shown above. Find the expression for ${a}_{0}.$

${a}_{0}=$ {{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
For our Fourier cosine series, the constant term is given by

$$
{a}_{0}=\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $f(x)=7{x}^{2}+4$ for $x\in (0,\pi ).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{0} & =\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }(7{x}^{2}+4)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }{[\frac{7{x}^{3}}{3}+4x]}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }(\frac{7{\pi }^{3}}{3}+4\pi )-0 \\  & =\frac{2}{3}(7{\pi }^{2}+12).\end{aligned}
$$
